keyAssumptions: ROSTER BASIS: CBRE's IN-PLACE PRO-FORMA for calendar year 2027 (page 9), which is what the $2,272,874 in-place NOI, the $1,164,153 recovery line and the $3,464,543 effective gross revenue tie to. This OM prints FULL lease dates (MM/DD/YY). Where the page-4 site plan shows a lower CURRENT rate, that rate is recorded in each tenant's rentSchedule.

Four-way tie-out against the OM's printed totals: (a) 156,316 SF occupied + 984 SF vacant = 157,300 SF GLA; (b) 156,316 / 157,300 = 99.4% occupancy; (c) base rents sum to $2,298,190 vs the $2,298,191 printed (rounding); (d) $3,464,543 EGR - $1,191,670 OpEx = $2,272,873 vs the $2,272,874 NOI printed (rounding). Tenant recoveries sum to $1,164,153 exactly.

TWO HEADLINE FIGURES DIFFER, AS DESIGNED: page 9's in-place EGR is $3,464,543 with NO general vacancy loss, producing the $2,272,874 headline NOI, while page 10's CY2027 cash flow applies a $23,702 general vacancy loss for $3,440,841 of EGR and $2,249,171 of NOI. The $2,272,874 in-place figure is recorded as the deal NOI and the CY2027 cash-flow row carries the $2,249,171. The 1.0% difference is the vacancy-loss factor, not an error.

WALT computes to 3.95 years from the roster's CURRENT-TERM expiries SF-weighted as of 01/01/2027, reproducing the OM's stated +/-4.0 years. Note this excludes ACME's five remaining five-year options (to a potential 2055) and Planet Fitness's one remaining option (to ~2034) — option-inclusive term is far longer than 4.0 years.

PAGE 3'S ANCHOR-REVENUE LABEL IS MISLEADING. It reads '29.6% Anchor Revenue / ACME Markets (29.6%) / Planet Fitness (13.5%)'. The arithmetic is: ACME $559,189 = 16.1% of revenue, Planet Fitness $465,622 = 13.4%, COMBINED 29.6%. ACME alone is not 29.6%.

ACME IS A GROUND LEASE at $2.59/SF on 42% of the GLA — the tenant owns its building. Its economics run through the recovery line ($387,972, 69% of its total revenue) rather than base rent, which is why the center's $14.70/SF weighted-average base rent understates the income intensity of the asset. There is no building mark-to-market on a ground lease; the five undisclosed option rents are what govern income after November 2030.

THE STARBUCKS AND COLD STONE PAD IS SEPARATELY PARCELED, which is why those two tenants carry recoveries of $38.84/SF and $33.98/SF — four to five times the center's $8.00-$8.82/SF shop rate. The pad pays its own New Jersey real-estate tax bill and it flows straight through. Their all-in occupancy costs are $97.19/SF and $70.83/SF respectively, and BOTH LEASES EXPIRE IN 2027.

MBM SPORTS APPEARS ON TWO ROWS AND THAT IS CORRECT, NOT A DUPLICATE: suite 005 (5,000 SF at $18.20/SF) and suite 005A (2,700 SF at $1.48/SF with zero recovery), both expiring February 2029. The $1.48/SF rate on 1.7% of the GLA reads as storage, mezzanine or non-selling ancillary area that is nonetheless counted in the 157,300 SF — verify what it is, because it flatters both the occupancy percentage and any price-per-foot calculation.

TWO LEASES COMMENCE ON 1 JANUARY 2027 — Bar Forno ($103,034) and Kleen Kar Car Wash ($48,000) — the first day of the analysis period. Together that is $151,034, or 6.6% of base rent, that is NOT in-place income today. Confirm both spaces are delivered and both tenants are open and paying before crediting it.
NO PRICE AND NO CAP RATE are quoted — unpriced marketing package. Value must be underwritten off the $2,272,874 in-place NOI.

TAXES ARE NOT REASSESSED, AND THIS IS NEW JERSEY WITH THE HEAVIEST TAX LOAD IN THIS PORTFOLIO GROUP. The $767,111 CY2027 real-estate tax line is $4.88/SF — 64% of total operating expenses and 34% of NOI — and the OM states expressly that reassessment is the investor's responsibility. New Jersey municipalities revalue on their own schedules and a sale commonly draws the assessor's attention; confirm Washington Township's revaluation status and the property's assessment-to-true-value ratio before bidding. The mitigant is that recoveries are strong here (98% of operating expenses), so most of an increase would pass through — but not on ACME's NNN+5% structure or on the tenants with below-rate recoveries.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT, and ACME's are expressly described as ANECDOTAL ($24.7 million, $374 PSF). The ±556,000 and ±469,400 customer-visit figures are Placer.ai traffic counts, not sales.

The OM does not print a year built, a renovation year, individual rent steps, renewal-option terms other than ACME's and Planet Fitness's, or any co-tenancy, exclusive or kickout clause. All left null rather than estimated. No footer date stamp appears on the Washington Center pro-forma pages, so omDate is left null (the sister Project Evergreen books are stamped July-August 2026).

redFlags.description: 80% OF GLA IS ROLLED BY THE END OF 2030, AND 75,374 SF ROLLS IN 2030 ALONE. ACME's ground lease (66,046 SF), Sherwin-Williams, Leslie's Pool Supplies and Chipotle all reach term in 2030, and Planet Fitness (20,742 SF) plus Mavis and both MBM suites reach term in 2029 — CBRE's own schedule shows 33,617 SF in 2029 and 75,374 SF in 2030, cumulative 80.12%. ACME's five five-year options and Planet Fitness's one option make renewal likely, but the OM prints NONE of the option rents, so the income beyond 2030 on 55% of the GLA is governed by terms this book does not disclose. Get both leases before bidding.

PLANET FITNESS HAS ONLY ONE OPTION LEFT. The current term ends September 2029 and a single five-year option would carry it to roughly 2034 — after which a 20,742 SF box with heavy gym build-out has no contractual protection at all. It is 13.4% of revenue and, by the OM's own account, an exceptional store, but the term structure is thin for an asset being marketed on 'highly durable income.'

THE 2027 EXPIRIES ARE CONCENTRATED IN THE HIGHEST-RENT, MOST STRETCHED SUITES. H&R Block (April 2027, $29.38/SF, seasonal), Debears Jewelers (May 2027), Cold Stone Creamery (June 2027, $70.83/SF all-in), Starbucks (August 2027, $97.19/SF all-in), Today's Cleaners and Taylor's Salon (both December 2027). That is 8,090 SF and roughly $276,000 of base rent, and CBRE's in-place NOI assumes every one of them simply holds over at current rents with no downtime or re-leasing cost. Starbucks and Cold Stone together are the entire separately-parceled pad — losing both would empty it at once.

NEW JERSEY TAXES ARE $767,111 — $4.88/SF, 64% of operating expenses and 34% of NOI — and are expressly NOT reassessed. This is the heaviest tax load in the portfolio group by a wide margin. A Washington Township revaluation or a post-sale assessment increase is the single largest quantifiable risk to the NOI, partially mitigated by strong recoveries but not on ACME's lighter NNN+5% structure.

$151,034 OF CY2027 BASE RENT (6.6%) COMES FROM TWO LEASES THAT COMMENCE ON THE FIRST DAY OF THE ANALYSIS PERIOD — Bar Forno ($103,034) and the Kleen Kar Car Wash ground lease ($48,000), both dated 1 January 2027. None of it is in-place income today. Confirm delivery, opening and rent commencement, and ask what free rent or landlord work sits behind those rates.

CHEF CHUN PAYS $35.84/SF, 43% ABOVE CBRE'S OWN $25.00/SF MARKET ASSUMPTION, with no sales disclosed, and expires March 2028. Above-market rent on a near-term expiry inflates the NOI a buyer capitalizes and can reset DOWN at renewal. The same pattern, more mildly, applies to H&R Block at $29.38/SF on a seasonal use.

NO SALES ARE DISCLOSED FOR ANY TENANT, and the anchor's are ANECDOTAL by the OM's own word ($24.7 million, $374 PSF). The impressive ±556,000 and ±469,400 figures are foot-traffic counts, not sales. Tenant health across a 157,300 SF center cannot be assessed from this book.

MBM Sports' 2,700 SF suite 005A pays $1.48/SF with zero recovery. If that space is storage or mezzanine rather than leasable retail, it is inflating the 157,300 SF GLA — which in turn flatters the 99.4% occupancy figure and understates any price-per-square-foot. Verify the measurement.

Leslie's Pool Supplies (3,440 SF) is a public company under real financial strain that has been closing stores; Rudi's Formal Wear is in a structurally declining category; and Today's Cleaners brings dry-cleaning environmental diligence. None is large, but all three warrant specific attention.

The 27,031 SF of pad sites the OM flags for 'parcelization and spin-off' is presented as clean optionality, but NO purchase option, right of first refusal or right of first offer is disclosed for Bank of America, McDonald's-style ground tenants or any pad. Ground leases on bank and QSR pads frequently carry an ROFR that would block a sale. Read the leases before crediting that value.

upsideItems.item: Parcelize and spin off the 27,031 SF of pad sites
upsideItems.detail: The 27,031 SF of pad sites with dedicated parking and pristine visibility is the headline lever: parcelize and spin off individual pads into the single-tenant net-lease market, where a Bank of America ground lease to 2036, a Chipotle to 2030 and a First Watch to 2031 each trade materially tighter than a South Jersey community center. The Starbucks/Cold Stone 3,050 SF pad is ALREADY separately parceled, which proves the mechanics work here. Confirm no ROFRs block a sale.

upsideItems.item: Bank of America ground lease to 2036 at $200,000
upsideItems.detail: Bank of America is the single largest base rent at $200,000 (8.7% of the total) on a 3,800 SF ground-leased pad running to July 2036 with investment-grade credit — the most valuable, most separable income in the deal.

upsideItems.item: ACME's five options run to a potential 2055
upsideItems.detail: ACME holds FIVE remaining five-year options to a potential 2055 on 42% of the GLA, with ±556,000 annual visits, anecdotal sales of $24.7 million ($374 PSF) at a computed 2.26% occupancy cost, beating the next-closest ACME by ±22,000 visits. That is exceptional term security — provided the option rents, which the OM does not print, are acceptable.

upsideItems.item: Planet Fitness is top-20% nationally by chain
upsideItems.detail: Planet Fitness ranks in the TOP 20% NATIONALLY by chain and is the busiest of six within ten miles, with ±469,400 annual visits — a genuinely outperforming box, which is the best argument that its one remaining option gets exercised.

Real shop mark-to-market on the 2029-2030 roll: Sherwin-Williams at $19.00/SF and Leslie's Pool Supplies at $19.57/SF against CBRE's $25.00/SF assumption, plus Banh Mi Factory at $17.00/SF. In-place rent is $14.70/SF against a $18.35/SF 2027 weighted-average market rent — a 25% aggregate gap on a functionally full center, captured through renewals rather than lease-up.

An exceptionally strong trade area: 149,910 people and 54,866 households with a $130,247 average household income, and within three miles $137,604 average and $116,957 median household income — the highest in this entire portfolio group. High income AND high density together justify the above-average rents, support a tighter going-in cap, and mark this as a supply-constrained infill location rather than a suburban strip.

Remarkable tenure and stability: a 21.8-year average operating tenure, with nearly 55% of the GLA in occupancy for over 25 years and 70% for more than 15 — and 63.2% of revenue from e-commerce-resistant tenants (dining, fitness, grocery, services, automotive).
Functionally full at 99.4% leased with a single 984 SF vacancy — no lease-up risk, no vacancy carry, and no speculative absorption assumption underpinning the projections.

upsideItems.item: Rowan University and the Route 42 corridor
upsideItems.detail: Rowan University (±24,500 enrolled) sits within the 5-mile ring alongside Gloucester Premium Outlets, and the center's position between NJ Route 42 and Hurffville-Cross Keys Road captures both daily commuters and seasonal shore traffic.

deals.notes: Washington Center Shoppes is a 157,300 SF grocery-anchored community center on 28.9 acres at Egg Harbor Road and Greentree Road in Sewell, New Jersey, between Route 42 and Hurffville-Cross Keys Road in the Philadelphia MSA, offered unpriced by CBRE within the Project Evergreen portfolio. It is the largest and highest-quality asset in this group: 99.4% leased with a single 984 SF vacancy, $2,272,874 of CY2027 in-place NOI on $3,464,543 of effective gross revenue, a 21.8-year average tenant tenure with 55% of the GLA in place more than 25 years, and the strongest demographics in the portfolio at $137,604 average household income within three miles and $130,247 across a 149,910-person trade area. ACME Markets anchors 42% of the GLA on a GROUND LEASE at $2.59/SF — the tenant owns its building, so its economics run through $387,972 of recoveries rather than rent — with anecdotal sales of $24.7 million, ±556,000 annual visits and five remaining five-year options to a potential 2055. Planet Fitness, the busiest of six within ten miles and top 20% nationally by chain, holds 20,742 SF to September 2029 with one option left. The tenancy underneath is genuinely good — Chipotle, Starbucks, First Watch, Bank of America on a ground lease at $200,000, Jersey Mike's, Mavis, Sherwin-Williams — and 63.2% of revenue comes from e-commerce-resistant uses. The clearest lever is the 27,031 SF of pad sites with dedicated parking that the OM flags for parcelization and spin-off into the single-tenant net-lease market, a mechanic already proven here by the separately-parceled Starbucks/Cold Stone pad. Three things need work before pricing. Eighty percent of the GLA is rolled by the end of 2030, including ACME and Planet Fitness, and the OM prints none of their option rents. The New Jersey tax line is $767,111 — $4.88/SF, 34% of NOI — and is expressly not reassessed. And the first-year expiries cluster in the most stretched suites, with Starbucks at a $97.19/SF all-in cost and Cold Stone at $70.83/SF both rolling in 2027 off the same separately-parceled pad, while $151,034 of 2027 base rent comes from two leases that commence on the very first day of the projection.
